rule.description: A class method whose consumed member-chain data accesses reachable through one container field of its own class (this.<holder>..., including holder aliases and destructuring reads rooted at the holder) dominate the method's own state and every other holder combined, with enough distinct leaves.

checks.description: Detect class methods whose data-access events through one container field (this.<holder>..., holder aliases, and destructuring reads rooted at the holder) dominate their own state and all other holders combined.
checks.detected_relation: class method -> foreign record held by a container field of the class
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The method is primarily interested in the data of the record it reaches through rather than in the state of the class it belongs to; the behavior belongs with the data it reads.

matches.evidence: Method reads this.info.data.authors, this.info.data.name, and this.info.data.description to derive the card label, sublabel, and description; the class holds no state beyond the record.

Method builds all three overflow actions from this.info: refetch reads id and selected, copy reads id, and the delete confirmation reads the record's name, removes it by id, and reverts the applied selection through the record.
Method derives the card title, icon lookup, and joined author names entirely from this.plugin.name, this.plugin.icon, and this.plugin.authors.
Method builds the author roster (display names, author identifiers, total) entirely from this.plugin.name and this.plugin.authors.
Method derives the repository card's title, byline, version label, and description entirely from this.manifest.display and this.manifest.version.

excluded.reason: Its methods read their own subscription registry through this; the holder groups neither reach the event threshold nor dominate own state, so the relation does not hold there.
Lifecycle methods read a small number of fields on their own state holder; no foreign record reached through a container field dominates the method.
